scenes.title: Standards are for the next reader
scenes.accessibleDescription: Judge whether another person can understand and change the software.

scenes.title: A failed save must look like a failure
scenes.accessibleDescription: Compare the visitor’s impression with what actually happened.

scenes.title: Test the edges of the system
scenes.accessibleDescription: Check where information enters, leaves, and changes state.

scenes.title: A slice includes its proof
scenes.accessibleDescription: A saved revision is useful, but it is not proof by itself.

scenes.title: Four observations, four different claims
scenes.accessibleDescription: Treat these as distinct evidence types, not an automatic ladder.

scenes.title: Keep evidence and recovery inspectable
scenes.accessibleDescription: A review record should reveal both confidence and gaps.

scenes.title: Make the code explain its purpose
scenes.accessibleDescription: Future diagnosis starts with names and responsibilities.

scenes.title: Give the right person the right error
scenes.accessibleDescription: Visitor feedback and operator diagnostics serve different jobs.

scenes.title: Prove the forbidden effects stay absent
scenes.accessibleDescription: A successful example cannot cover every important boundary.

scenes.title: Where was the claim tested?
scenes.accessibleDescription: Match the environment to the observation.

scenes.title: Review one coherent change
scenes.accessibleDescription: Ask focused questions while the change is small enough to assess.

scenes.title: Write a record someone else can inspect
scenes.accessibleDescription: A useful evidence note contains context rather than confidence alone.

scenes.title: Ask to see the observation
scenes.accessibleDescription: Replace broad quality claims with specific evidence.
